title: Structured velocity field in the inner envelope of B335: ALMA observations of rare CO isotopologues
question: Investigate the molecular line velocity profiles of the Class 0 protostar B335 and constrain the infall motions in its circumstellar gas, in particular the origin of double-peaked C17O profiles

data.angular_resolution: Beam 2.6 x 1.9 arcsec (C17O, 12CO after smoothing), 2.7 x 2.0 arcsec (C18O)

what.value: H2 peak column density 3.1e22 cm^-2 at 3600 au, used for the opacity estimate

evidence.quote: 3.1 $\times$ 10$^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$ is the peak column density of H$_{2}$ in B335 at a radius of 3600 au ((cite: Launhardt2013))

what.value: C17O abundance relative to H2 of 5e-8

evidence.quote: = 5 $\times$ 10$^{-8}$ is the C$^{17}$O abundance relative to H$_{2}$ abundance ((cite: Thomas2008))

what.value: Einstein coefficient A10 = 6.695e-8 s^-1 for C17O J=1-0

evidence.quote: is the Einstein coefficient for the C$^{17}$O J = 1–0 transition ((cite: Hitran2017), (cite: Splatalogue2005))

evidence.quote: C$^{18}$O is a factor of 3.6-3.9 more abundant than C$^{17}$O ((cite: Penzias1981), (cite: Jorgensen2002))

which we adapted to the new distance of 164.5 pc

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image the lines
recipe.method: Standard cycle-4 calibration in CASA, continuum self-calibration, tCLEAN imaging with Briggs weighting, 12CO smoothed to the C17O/C18O resolution
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 2 for C17O and C18O, robust = 1 for 12CO
C17O/C18O maps from C40-2 only; 12CO from two configurations combined

recipe.method: Moment 0 maps of C17O and 12CO; C17O spectra extracted at every 0.5 arcsec pixel to build a spectral map
key_parameters: Mean radius of 3 sigma C17O emission is 860 au

recipe.goal: Estimate maximum C17O line opacity from column density
recipe.method: Opacity tau0 from A10, nu, peak H2 column density, C17O abundance and linewidth (Jansen 1995 formula)
key_parameters: Delta V approx 1 km/s average linewidth of the two components together
assumptions: H2 column density 3.1e22 cm^-2 (peak at 3600 au) and C17O abundance 5e-8

recipe.goal: Compare C17O and C18O integrated intensities
recipe.method: Beam-matched C17O and C18O maps; ratio of integrated intensities W(C17O)/W(C18O) compared with the optically thin expectation from abundances
key_parameters: Integration ranges: C17O 4.8-6.2 and 7.4-9.4 km/s (two hyperfine components); C18O 7.4-9.4 km/s
assumptions: C17O and C18O probe similar conditions; differences arise only from opacity; no fractionation or selective photodissociation

recipe.goal: Fit two-component hyperfine model to C17O spectra
recipe.method: HfS fit per pixel with two velocity components (blue and red), giving velocity, linewidth and opacity maps
key_parameters: Per component, four free parameters: linewidth (shared by hyperfine components), main line central velocity, main line peak intensity, optical depth
Minimum signal-to-noise of 3 sigma for fitting
assumptions: C17O (1-0) expected to be optically thin

recipe.goal: Kinetic temperature, thermal and non-thermal linewidths
recipe.method: Tk(r) from a central-heating temperature profile at 100 and 860 au; thermal linewidth for C17O (29.01 amu); non-thermal part from v_obs^2 = v_th^2 + v_nonth^2
key_parameters: Radii 100 au (about half the FWHM beam) to 860 au
assumptions: Dust and gas in thermal equilibrium, coupled by collisions at densities above 1e5 cm^-3

recipe.goal: Estimate free-fall velocity difference between 100 and 860 au
recipe.method: Difference of free-fall velocities v_ff(r1) - v_ff(r2) with enclosed mass = envelope mass (from 110 GHz continuum) plus central object mass
key_parameters: Central object mass 0.05-0.26 Msun adopted from infall models
assumptions: Maximum velocity difference along the line of sight occurs at the core center; envelope mass uses standard dust assumptions

recipe.goal: Estimate flux missed by the interferometer
recipe.method: ALMA C18O map smoothed to the Nobeyama 45 m beam, spectrum over one beam, flux converted to brightness temperature (Rayleigh-Jeans) and compared with single-dish data; C17O missing flux then inferred to be smaller
assumptions: C17O is much more compact than C18O so its missing flux is smaller
